title: Design an Enterprise RAG System at Scale (10M+ Documents with ACLs)
prompt: Design an enterprise RAG platform indexing 10M+ multi-format documents (~150M chunks) from Drive, Confluence, and Git with incremental CDC permission sync, < 500 ms retrieval + rerank latency, zero cross-tenant/ACL leaks, and inline citation verification.

spark.summary: Ingest documents via incremental CDC connectors into sharded Qdrant/Milvus + Elasticsearch BM25 with synced Roaring Bitmap ACLs, fuse via RRF, rerank Top-50 -> Top-5, and verify LLM citations.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, sync document ACL changes independently from re-embedding chunks so permission revocations take effect in seconds without recomputing 150M vectors.
spark.byteSummary:
At 10M documents (~150M 512-token chunks), re-embedding an entire folder just because one user lost Google Drive access would crush GPU pipelines. Decouple **Chunk Vector Storage** from **ACL Metadata** (storing `allowed_principals` in a fast-update payload/bitmap index synced via CDC webhooks).

On query, the gateway resolves the user's transitive Okta/AD group memberships (cached 60s), executes ACL-prefiltered HNSW + BM25 search across sharded Qdrant/Elasticsearch nodes, merges Top-50 via RRF, and reranks to Top-5 with a GPU Cross-Encoder.

The LLM synthesizes the answer with mandatory `[doc_id:span]` citations, checked by a lightweight NLI entailment gate to catch unsupported claims.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design an Enterprise RAG System at Scale (10M+ Documents with ACLs) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, sync document ACL changes independently from re-embedding chunks so permission revocations take effect in seconds without recomputing 150M vectors.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.
